newsitem.title: UK: British Airways faces more strikes-papers.
newsitem.headline: British Airways faces more strikes-papers.

text.p: British Airways faces the threat of another strike this week after cabin crew involved in last week's three-day stoppage were ordered home without pay, union officials said on Monday.
Leaders of the 9,000 cabin crew said they could mount another 72-hour stoppage if the suspension of around 100 employees was not lifted by 1400 GMT on Monday.
The airline denied it had suspended strikers but said anyone who had stopped work last week had to give a commitment to work normally and then wait at home to be rostered for work.
"There can be no talks while there are suspensions," union representative George Ryde told the Independent newspaper. "This is pure stupidity."

British Airways flight schedules are still affected by the dispute over pay and conditions following a company plan to save 42 million pounds ($71.20 million) as a part of a drive to improve competitiveness.
The strike ended early on Saturday but the airline was able to operate only 70 percent of its intercontinental flights out of London's Heathrow airport, its main hub, on Sunday.
Around 45 percent of BA's European and 40 percent of its domestic services took off from Heathrow. At Gatwick airport south of London, BA operated 89 percent of long-haul departures.
On Monday, BA expects to run 85 percent of long-haul flights, 60 percent of European flights and more than half of its domestic services.
Out of Gatwick, the airline would operate almost 95 percent of flights, and full service was expected to be restored on Tuesday, BA said. ($1=.5899 Pound)
